tagline: A railroad village that grew 8× in thirty years — and built itself a downtown instead of sprawling.
summary: A railroad village of a few thousand people as late as 1990, Suwanee grew eightfold in thirty years. Instead of sprawling, it built a walkable town center in the 2000s and has kept adding parks to it. Most families come for the North Gwinnett schools.

rankings.title: Best Places to Live for Families
rankings.detail: Fortune, 2024 — #27 in the U.S. of about 2,000 cities considered; the top Georgia city on the list.

rankings.title: North Gwinnett High School
rankings.detail: U.S. News Best High Schools, 2025–26 · #21 of 458 Georgia high schools on SchoolDigger.

rows.label: Adults with a bachelor's or higher

history.text: A Shawnee village; the name is usually traced to the Creek word for Shawnee.
The Air Line Railroad builds a depot — the village grows around it.
Incorporated as a city; still farmland into the 1970s.
Home base of the Atlanta Falcons' training facility.
Town Center Park and the new City Hall are built — a downtown on purpose.
Town Center on Main opens: a 13-acre park beside the library.

education.note: North Gwinnett: #16 in Georgia (U.S. News 2025–26), Niche A+, GreatSchools 10/10. Suwanee's 30024 ZIP is also served by Collins Hill (Gwinnett) and Lambert (Forsyth). District rate: AJC, 2021. Which school a home is zoned for depends on its address.

planning.title: 2040 Comprehensive Plan (2019)
planning.text: Most new building is to be infill at medium density; the city is mapped into 11 character areas, each with its own rules.

planning.title: Suwanee Gateway · I-85
planning.text: An aging interstate interchange slated to become a Class-A office district with hotels.

planning.title: Town Center on Main · 2024
planning.text: A 13-acre park and DeLay Nature Park on a 25-acre site, with a rebuilt PlayTown playground.

planning.title: 2040 Strategic Plan
planning.text: A broader city strategy, expected to be adopted in late 2026.

frames.headline: Suwanee
frames.say: This is Suwanee, Georgia — Fortune's top city in the state for families, thirty-three miles from downtown Atlanta.

frames.headline: A railroad town

rows.v: A depot on the Air Line Railroad — the village grows around it
Home of the Atlanta Falcons' training camp
Town Center Park and City Hall are built

frames.say: It grew around an 1871 railroad depot, became a city in 1949, and once housed the Atlanta Falcons.

frames.headline: 8.6× since 1990
frames.say: Since 1990 its population has grown more than eightfold, to about twenty-one thousand.

frames.headline: Above the state

stats.label: of adults hold a bachelor's degree — 1.8× Georgia's

frames.say: Incomes run a third above the state's, and nearly two in three adults hold a degree.

frames.headline: North Gwinnett High

stats.label: in Georgia — U.S. News Best High Schools, 2025–26

frames.say: Families come for the schools: North Gwinnett High ranks sixteenth in Georgia and graduates ninety-five percent.

frames.headline: On the I-85 corridor
frames.say: Interstate 85 is minutes away — downtown in about forty minutes off-peak, the airport in under an hour.

frames.headline: Growth, on purpose

rows.v: Town Center on Main — a 13-acre park beside the library
Suwanee Gateway — an office district planned at the interchange
Comprehensive plan — infill at medium density

frames.say: And it grows on purpose: a new thirteen-acre park in 2024, an office district planned at the interstate.

places.say: Downtown, a section of the Berlin Wall stands in Town Center Park, home of Suwanee Fest each September.
Next door, the library anchors Town Center on Main, the city's newest park.
The Suwanee Creek Greenway runs about four miles through woods and wetland.
Sims Lake Park is the quiet one: a lake loop, a pier, a pavilion over the water.
Dinner is steps from the green, on the patio at Tequila Mama.
StillFire Brewing is steps from Town Center, with its patio out front.
North Gwinnett High School is two miles from Town Center.
Everyday errands and a few restaurants are at Suwanee Jubilee, two miles out.
